name: 1941 Southeast Asia & Western Pacific Land Airfields (Combined)

metadata.timeframe: Late 1941 (Eve of the Pacific War, December 1941)
metadata.geographic_scope: Southeast Asia & Western Pacific: Philippines, British Malaya & Singapore, Borneo (Sarawak & Dutch Kalimantan), Dutch East Indies (Java, Sumatra, Sulawesi, Lesser Sundas, Moluccas, Dutch New Guinea) & Portuguese Timor, French Indochina, and Thailand (Siam)
metadata.facility_scope: Land airfields only (seaplane bases and flying-boat water anchorages excluded)
primary_sources: London Gazette Supplement (1948), Report on RAF Operations in Malaya and N.E.I. 1941-42, Appendix A (Situation at RAF Stations in Malaya, 8 Dec 1941)
USAAF Far East Air Force (FEAF) & Philippine Department Air Force 1941 Order of Battle and Airfield Summaries (US Army CMH / USAF Historical Studies)
Militaire Luchtvaart van het KNIL (ML-KNIL) 30 Nov 1941 Order of Battle & KNILM 1938-1941 Civil Route Network Records
U.S. War Department, A Survey of Thailand (Siam) (March 1941), Appendix I (Airdromes and Landing Grounds) & Royal Thai Air Force Historical Archives
Vichy French Armee de l'Air & Imperial Japanese Southern French Indochina Occupation Records (1940-1941)
metadata.title: 1941 Southeast Asia & Western Pacific Land Airfields (Combined)

properties.name: Clark Field
properties.runway_notes_1941: Multiple graded grass/sod strips; main Luzon heavy bomber field
properties.notes: HQ 5th Bomber Command, 19th Bomb Group (B-17C/D) & 24th Pursuit Group (20th PS P-40B); devastated in 8 Dec 1941 air raid.
properties.title: Clark Field

properties.name: Nichols Field
properties.runway_notes_1941: Concrete runway under completion late 1941 — only hard-surfaced military runway in PH
properties.notes: Base of 17th & 21st Pursuit Squadrons (P-40E), 2d Observation Squadron, and Philippine Air Depot.
properties.modern_equivalent: Ninoy Aquino International Airport / Villamor Air Base (MNL / RPLL)
properties.title: Nichols Field

properties.name: Nielson Field
properties.operator_1941: USAAF FEAF HQ / Philippine Air Lines (pre-Oct 1941)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Intersecting paved runways in Makati (modern Ayala & Paseo de Roxas avenues)
properties.notes: Opened 1937 as Manila's premier commercial airport (PATCO/PAL); commandeered in Oct 1941 as Far East Air Force HQ.
properties.title: Nielson Field

properties.name: Zablan Field
properties.operator_1941: Philippine Army Air Corps (inducted into USAAF FEAF)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Graded grass strip adjacent to Camp Murphy
properties.notes: First Philippine Army Air Corps airfield (opened 1935); home to 6th Pursuit Squadron (Boeing P-26A) in Dec 1941.
properties.modern_equivalent: Defunct (Camp General Emilio Aguinaldo, Quezon City)
properties.title: Zablan Field

properties.name: Iba Field
properties.runway_notes_1941: Coastal sandy/dirt pursuit strip on Zambales shore
properties.notes: Base of 3d Pursuit Squadron (P-40E) and Luzon's sole operational SCR-270 early-warning radar; destroyed 8 Dec 1941.
properties.title: Iba Field

properties.name: Del Carmen Field
properties.runway_notes_1941: Newly graded dirt pursuit strip (~4,500 ft); dusty conditions
properties.notes: Constructed 1941 by 803rd Engineer Aviation Bn as Clark satellite; base of 34th Pursuit Squadron (P-35A).
properties.title: Del Carmen Field

properties.name: Rosales Field
properties.runway_notes_1941: Graded dirt dispersal strip on Lingayen Plain
properties.notes: Constructed in 1941 as northern Luzon heavy bomber/pursuit dispersal airfield.
properties.title: Rosales Field

properties.name: O'Donnell Field
properties.runway_notes_1941: Auxiliary dirt strip constructed Nov-Dec 1941
properties.notes: Built by Company A, 803rd Engineer Aviation Bn northwest of Clark Field as dispersal strip.
properties.title: O'Donnell Field

properties.name: San Marcelino Field
properties.runway_notes_1941: Auxiliary dirt pursuit strip northwest of Subic Bay
properties.notes: Begun in Nov 1941 as pursuit dispersal strip; later expanded during 1945 campaign.
properties.title: San Marcelino Field

properties.name: Bataan Field
properties.runway_notes_1941: 2,000-ft dirt strip graded early 1941 (lengthened to 5,100 ft late Dec 1941)
properties.notes: Originally dubbed 'Richards' Folly' on Manila Bay side of Bataan; became primary fighter strip during the Siege of Bataan.
properties.title: Bataan Field

properties.name: Maniquis Field
properties.runway_notes_1941: Grass military training and auxiliary landing field near Camp Ord
properties.notes: Pre-war PAAC/US Army auxiliary airfield serving San Miguel / Tarlac training area.
properties.title: Maniquis Field

properties.name: Batangas Field
properties.runway_notes_1941: Graded grass/dirt military landing field north of Batangas town
properties.notes: Pre-war PAAC field; 6th Pursuit Squadron P-26A fighters engaged Japanese aircraft here on 12 Dec 1941.
properties.title: Batangas Field

properties.name: Del Monte Field No. 1
properties.runway_notes_1941: Heavy bomber sod meadow runway on pineapple plantation, completed 4 Dec 1941
properties.notes: Strategic B-17 dispersal base in Bukidnon; 16 B-17s of 14th & 93d BS arrived 6 Dec 1941, escaping the Clark Field disaster.
properties.title: Del Monte Field No. 1

properties.name: Kindley Field
properties.operator_1941: US Army (Harbor Defenses of Manila & Subic Bays)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Short (~2,000 ft) graded dirt liaison strip on Corregidor's eastern tail
properties.notes: Constructed in the 1920s for Army courier and observation aircraft supporting Fort Mills.
properties.title: Kindley Field

properties.name: Plaridel Field
properties.runway_notes_1941: Graded grass auxiliary/liaison strip north of Manila
properties.notes: Pre-war liaison and emergency landing field in Bulacan along the central Luzon corridor.
properties.title: Plaridel Field

properties.name: Grace Park Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Grass/dirt commercial field north of Manila
properties.notes: Opened in 1935 as one of Manila's earliest commercial airports, used by INAEC, flying schools, and civil charter operators.
properties.title: Grace Park Airfield

properties.name: Loakan Airport (Baguio)
properties.operator_1941: Philippine Air Lines (PAL) / Commonwealth Bureau of Aeronautics
properties.runway_notes_1941: High-elevation mountain runway (~4,250 ft ASL)
properties.notes: Opened 1934; destination of Philippine Air Lines' inaugural commercial flight on 15 Mar 1941; bombed 8 Dec 1941.
properties.title: Loakan Airport (Baguio)

properties.name: Laoag (Gabu) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Coastal graded sand/grass landing field
properties.notes: Pre-war northern Luzon commercial landing field; rapidly seized by Japanese forces in Dec 1941 for forward fighter ops.
properties.title: Laoag (Gabu) Airfield

properties.name: Aparri Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Coastal grass/dirt landing ground near Cagayan River mouth
properties.notes: Pre-war civil landing field on Luzon's northern coast; primary objective of Japanese Tanaka Detachment landing on 10 Dec 1941.
properties.title: Aparri Airfield

properties.name: Vigan (Mindoro) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Short coastal dirt landing ground southwest of Vigan
properties.notes: Pre-war Ilocos civil landing field; captured by Japanese landing force on 10 Dec 1941.
properties.title: Vigan (Mindoro) Airfield

properties.name: Tuguegarao Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Cagayan Valley grass/dirt landing field
properties.notes: Pre-war Cagayan Valley civil airfield opened in the 1930s; captured by Japan in Dec 1941.
properties.title: Tuguegarao Airfield

properties.name: Paracale Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Commercial dirt airstrip serving Camarines Norte gold-mining district
properties.notes: Active pre-war commercial gold-mining route destination served from Manila (Nielson Field).
properties.title: Paracale Airfield

properties.name: Legazpi Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war civil landing field at foot of Mount Mayon
properties.notes: Key southern Luzon commercial stop; captured by Japanese Kimura Detachment on 12 Dec 1941 for IJNAS Zero operations.
properties.title: Legazpi Airfield

properties.name: Naga Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Graded grass/dirt Bicol regional airfield
properties.notes: Pre-war Bicol Peninsula commercial airfield serving Naga and Camarines Sur.
properties.title: Naga Airfield

properties.name: Lahug Airfield (Cebu)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Graded grass/coral runway northeast of Cebu City
properties.notes: Opened in the 1930s as Cebu's main pre-war civil commercial airport; also used by PAAC and USAAF transit aircraft.
properties.modern_equivalent: Defunct (Cebu IT Park, Lahug, Cebu City)
properties.title: Lahug Airfield (Cebu)

properties.name: Mandurriao Airfield (Iloilo)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Commercial grass/dirt airport on Panay
properties.notes: Opened 1937 as headquarters and primary Visayan hub of INAEC (operating Stinson & Sikorsky aircraft).
properties.title: Mandurriao Airfield (Iloilo)

properties.name: Bacolod Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Commercial grass/dirt airport on Negros Occidental coast
properties.notes: Opened 1936 as INAEC's major Negros terminal connecting Bacolod, Iloilo, Cebu, and Manila.
properties.title: Bacolod Airfield

properties.name: Tacloban Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war sandy/coral strip on Cataisan Peninsula
properties.notes: Established in the late 1930s as Leyte's civil landing field; later famously expanded by US forces in Oct 1944.
properties.title: Tacloban Airfield

properties.name: San Jose (Mindoro) Airfield
properties.operator_1941: Commonwealth Bureau of Aeronautics / Philippine Milling Co.
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war civil/estate grass landing strip
properties.notes: Pre-war Mindoro commercial and sugar-estate landing field linking Manila and the western Visayas.
properties.title: San Jose (Mindoro) Airfield

properties.name: Puerto Princesa Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war Commonwealth civil landing ground on Palawan
properties.notes: Established pre-war for civil mail and administrative flights; later expanded into a major military base during WWII.
properties.title: Puerto Princesa Airfield

properties.name: Zamboanga (San Roque) Airfield
properties.operator_1941: Commonwealth Bureau of Aeronautics / USAAF auxiliary
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war coastal grass/dirt landing field
properties.notes: Key southwestern Mindanao civil and mail airport overlooking Basilan Strait; also used as military staging stop.
properties.title: Zamboanga (San Roque) Airfield

properties.name: Davao Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war commercial grass/dirt strip near Davao Gulf
properties.notes: Southern Mindanao commercial airport; captured by Japan on 20 Dec 1941 and used to launch attacks on the Dutch East Indies.
properties.title: Davao Airfield

properties.name: Cagayan de Misamis Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war civil landing field serving northern Mindanao coast
properties.notes: Pre-war commercial landing ground serving Cagayan de Misamis prior to expansion of nearby Del Monte bomber complex.
properties.title: Cagayan de Misamis Airfield

properties.name: Cotabato Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war central Mindanao grass landing field
properties.notes: Established in the 1930s for Commonwealth civil administrative and commercial air links in Cotabato.
properties.title: Cotabato Airfield

properties.name: Surigao Airfield
properties.operator_1941: Commonwealth Bureau of Aeronautics / Mining Charter
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war civil/mining dirt landing strip in NE Mindanao
properties.notes: Served pre-war Surigao gold-mining operations and inter-island commercial flights.
properties.title: Surigao Airfield

properties.name: RAF Seletar
properties.runway_notes_1941: Complete grass aerodrome: 1,400 yds (London Gazette App. A); major landplane & maintenance base
properties.notes: Primary RAF Far East station (opened 1928) hosting torpedo-bomber squadrons (Nos. 36 & 100 Sqns) and main aircraft depot. (Also had adjacent seaplane slipways; included here as a major landplane station.)
properties.title: RAF Seletar

properties.name: RAF Tengah
properties.runway_notes_1941: Concrete runway plus 1,400-yd grass landing ground (London Gazette App. A)
properties.notes: Opened 1939; main RAF bomber station on western Singapore Island (No. 34 Sqn Blenheims & Borneo GR reserve).
properties.title: RAF Tengah

properties.name: RAF Sembawang
properties.runway_notes_1941: Grass runway: 1,380 yds (hard runways deferred as of 8 Dec 1941)
properties.notes: Opened 1940 near Singapore Naval Base; HQ RAAF Far East and home to No. 453 Sqn RAAF Buffalos & No. 8 Sqn RAAF Hudsons.
properties.title: RAF Sembawang

properties.name: RAF Kota Bharu
properties.runway_notes_1941: Grass runway: 1,600 yds, being extended (London Gazette App. A)
properties.notes: Home to No. 1 Sqn RAAF Hudsons & No. 36 Sqn detachment; target of the opening Japanese amphibious assault of the Pacific War on 8 Dec 1941.
properties.title: RAF Kota Bharu

properties.name: RAF Gong Kedah
properties.runway_notes_1941: Hard-surfaced runway: 2,000 yds (London Gazette App. A)
properties.notes: Major forward bomber airfield in northeastern Malaya; bombed on 8 Dec 1941 and evacuated shortly after the Kota Bharu landing.
properties.title: RAF Gong Kedah

properties.name: RAF Machang
properties.runway_notes_1941: Hard-surfaced runway: 1,600 yds (2nd 1,200-yd strip in hand, London Gazette App. A)
properties.notes: Forward fighter concentration airfield in Kelantan; abandoned during the initial British withdrawal from northeast Malaya.
properties.title: RAF Machang

properties.name: RAF Alor Star
properties.runway_notes_1941: Hard-surfaced runway: 1,400 yds (London Gazette App. A)
properties.notes: Opened 1929 as civil aerodrome and expanded into major RAF bomber station (No. 62 Sqn Blenheims); heavily bombed 8 Dec 1941.
properties.title: RAF Alor Star

properties.name: RAF Sungei Patani
properties.runway_notes_1941: Two grass runways: 1,400 yds and 1,200 yds (London Gazette App. A)
properties.notes: Main northern fighter station; base of No. 21 Sqn RAAF Buffalos & No. 27 Sqn RAF Blenheim night fighters; bombed 8 Dec 1941.
properties.title: RAF Sungei Patani

properties.name: RAF Butterworth
properties.runway_notes_1941: Hard runway 1,600 yds being extended to 2,000 yds; 2nd runway in hand
properties.notes: Completed Oct 1941 for RAF/RAAF general reconnaissance and fighter defense of Penang; attacked 8 Dec 1941.
properties.title: RAF Butterworth

properties.name: RAF Kuala Ketil
properties.runway_notes_1941: Tarmac runway: 1,400 yds; guard room, POL & bomb stores (London Gazette App. A)
properties.notes: RAF dispersal satellite airfield for RAF Sungei Patani in southern Kedah.
properties.title: RAF Kuala Ketil

properties.name: RAF Jabi
properties.runway_notes_1941: 1,400 yds graded but not yet surfaced on 8 Dec 1941 (London Gazette App. A)
properties.notes: Forward NW Malaya bomber dispersal site east of Alor Star.
properties.title: RAF Jabi

properties.name: RAF Lubok Kiap
properties.runway_notes_1941: Hard runway 1,600 yds + 1,200 yds partly graded; hutments nearing completion
properties.notes: Newly built NW Malaya bomber station inland from Butterworth, partly occupied on 8 Dec 1941.
properties.modern_equivalent: Defunct (Lubok Kiap / Padang Serai area, Kedah)
properties.title: RAF Lubok Kiap

properties.name: RAF Malakoff
properties.runway_notes_1941: 1,600-yd strip, grading incomplete and no buildings on 8 Dec 1941
properties.notes: Satellite dispersal airfield for RAF Lubok Kiap on Malakoff Estate.
properties.title: RAF Malakoff

properties.name: RAF Sungei Bakap
properties.runway_notes_1941: 2,000-yd strip (1,400 yds soled but unsurfaced on 8 Dec 1941)
properties.notes: RAF satellite landing ground for RAF Butterworth in southern Province Wellesley.
properties.title: RAF Sungei Bakap

properties.name: RAF Kuantan
properties.runway_notes_1941: Two grass runways: 1,500 yds and 1,200 yds; accommodation for 2 squadrons
properties.notes: Key east-coast base (No. 8 Sqn RAAF Hudsons & No. 60 Sqn RAF Blenheims); heavily bombed 9 Dec 1941 just prior to the sinking of Force Z nearby.
properties.modern_equivalent: Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Airport / RMAF Kuantan (KUA / WMKD)
properties.title: RAF Kuantan

properties.name: RAF Kluang
properties.runway_notes_1941: Two grass runways: 1,600 yds & 1,200 yds; hard runway commenced
properties.notes: Major southern Malaya fighter/bomber concentration base in Johore; hosted RAF, RAAF, and reinforcing Dutch ML-KNIL units.
properties.title: RAF Kluang

properties.name: RAF Kahang
properties.runway_notes_1941: Two grass runways: 1,400 yds & 1,300 yds (London Gazette App. A)
properties.notes: General reconnaissance airfield in eastern Johore defending approaches from Mersing and Endau.
properties.title: RAF Kahang

properties.name: RAF Tebrau
properties.runway_notes_1941: Hard runway 1,200 yds (2nd 2,000-yd runway in hand, London Gazette App. A)
properties.notes: Southern Johore airfield immediately north of the Singapore Causeway.
properties.title: RAF Tebrau

properties.name: Kallang Airport
properties.operator_1941: Straits Settlements Civil Aviation / BOAC, Qantas, KNILM, Wearne's (RAF in Dec 1941)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Circular 1,000-yd / 1,400-yd grass civil aerodrome built on reclaimed Kallang Basin
properties.notes: Opened June 1937 as Singapore's flagship international civil airport; operated by RAF/RAAF fighter squadrons (Nos. 243 & 488 Sqns) during the defense of Singapore.
properties.modern_equivalent: Defunct (Kallang Basin / Old Kallang Airport Terminal preserved)
properties.title: Kallang Airport

properties.name: Penang (Bayan Lepas) Civil Aerodrome
properties.operator_1941: Straits Settlements Civil Aviation / Imperial Airways & Wearne's
properties.runway_notes_1941: Limited grass civil aerodrome (London Gazette App. A)
properties.notes: Opened 1935 as Penang's civil airport on the London-Singapore-Australia Empire air route.
properties.title: Penang (Bayan Lepas) Civil Aerodrome

properties.name: Kuala Lumpur (Sungai Besi) Civil Aerodrome
properties.operator_1941: FMS Civil Aviation / Wearne's (RAF No. 153 MU in 1941)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Grass civil aerodrome: 1,315 yds (London Gazette App. A)
properties.notes: Opened 1930 as Kuala Lumpur's civil airport; also housed RAF No. 153 Maintenance Unit from June 1941.
properties.modern_equivalent: Defunct (Bandar Malaysia / Former RMAF Sungai Besi, WMKF)
properties.title: Kuala Lumpur (Sungai Besi) Civil Aerodrome

properties.name: Ipoh Civil Aerodrome
properties.operator_1941: FMS Civil Aviation / Wearne's (RAF concentration base Dec 1941)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Grass plus tarmac runway: 1,400 yds; RAF hutments nearly complete
properties.notes: Opened 1937 as Perak civil airport serving Kinta Valley tin district; used by RAAF Nos. 21 & 453 Sqns during Dec 1941 retreat.
properties.title: Ipoh Civil Aerodrome

properties.name: Taiping (Tekah) Civil Aerodrome
properties.operator_1941: FMS Civil Aviation (RAF satellite for Ipoh in 1941)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Grass plus tarmac runway: 1,400 yds (London Gazette App. A)
properties.notes: Opened 1930 as Malaya's oldest civil aerodrome; served as RAF satellite dispersal strip for Ipoh in Dec 1941.
properties.title: Taiping (Tekah) Civil Aerodrome

properties.name: Sitiawan Civil Aerodrome
properties.runway_notes_1941: Two grass strips: 1,000 yds & 800 yds; guard room only (London Gazette App. A)
properties.notes: Pre-war civil landing field on Perak coast guarded by Indian State Troops.
properties.title: Sitiawan Civil Aerodrome

properties.name: Port Swettenham Civil Aerodrome
properties.runway_notes_1941: Grass strip with tarmac center: 1,000 yds (London Gazette App. A)
properties.notes: Pre-war civil landing ground serving Selangor's principal seaport (modern Port Klang).
properties.title: Port Swettenham Civil Aerodrome

properties.name: Batu Pahat Civil Aerodrome
properties.operator_1941: Johore Civil Aviation (RAF satellite for Kluang)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Grass runway: 1,400 yds; POL stores & AIF infantry guard (London Gazette App. A)
properties.notes: Pre-war Johore civil airfield designated as an RAF dispersal satellite for Kluang.
properties.title: Batu Pahat Civil Aerodrome

properties.name: Kuching Airfield (7th Mile)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Graded grass/laterite airfield 7 miles south of Kuching (opened 1938)
properties.notes: Principal airfield in British Borneo in Dec 1941; defended by 2/15th Punjab Regiment and captured by Japan on 25 Dec 1941.
properties.title: Kuching Airfield (7th Mile)

properties.name: Singkawang II Airfield (Ledo)
properties.operator_1941: ML-KNIL (Royal Netherlands East Indies Army Air Force)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Camouflaged secret jungle airbase near Sanggau Ledo
properties.notes: Pre-war ML-KNIL secret airfield near the Sarawak border; hosted Glenn Martin bombers and Brewster 339D fighters attacking Japanese convoys off Kuching in Dec 1941.
properties.modern_equivalent: Harry Hadisoemantri Air Force Base (Sanggau Ledo)
properties.title: Singkawang II Airfield (Ledo)

properties.name: Samarinda II Airfield (Melak)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Two camouflaged parallel jungle runways between Melak and Long Iram (begun 1940)
properties.notes: Remarkable secret ML-KNIL jungle base deep up the Mahakam River; hosted 2-VLG-I Martin bombers & 1-VLG-V Brewster fighters in Dec 1941.
properties.title: Samarinda II Airfield (Melak)

properties.name: Tarakan (Juata) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Graded oil-island airfield serving Tarakan oilfields
properties.notes: Hosted Patrouille Butner (1-VLG-I Martin bombers) and KNILM flights; primary target of Japanese invasion of Tarakan (Jan 1942).
properties.title: Tarakan (Juata) Airfield

properties.name: Balikpapan (Manggar) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Coastal airfield east of Balikpapan oil refineries
properties.notes: Protected Dutch Borneo's vital oil port and served KNILM civil routes; captured by Japan in Jan 1942.
properties.modern_equivalent: Sultan Aji Muhammad Sulaiman Sepinggan Airport (BPN / WALL)
properties.title: Balikpapan (Manggar) Airfield

properties.name: Banjarmasin (Ulin) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Completed 1936; strategic southern Borneo airfield
properties.notes: Major civil (KNILM) and military staging base directly opposite Java across the Java Sea.
properties.title: Banjarmasin (Ulin) Airfield

properties.name: Kotawaringin (Pangkalanbun) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war ML-KNIL dispersal airfield in southwestern Borneo
properties.notes: Constructed pre-war by Dutch colonial authorities as a staging and dispersal field linking Java and Borneo.
properties.title: Kotawaringin (Pangkalanbun) Airfield

properties.name: Miri / Lutong Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Coastal company/civil landing strip near Lutong oil refinery
properties.notes: Active pre-war oilfield landing ground; rendered unusable by British demolition teams on 9 Dec 1941 ahead of the 16 Dec Japanese landing.
properties.title: Miri / Lutong Airfield

properties.name: Bintulu Landing Ground
properties.runway_notes_1941: Coastal grass/dirt emergency strip (begun 1934, work paused 1938)
properties.notes: One of only three pre-war airfields in all of British Borneo (alongside Kuching and Miri).
properties.title: Bintulu Landing Ground

properties.name: Pontianak (Sungai Durian) Airfield
properties.operator_1941: KNILM / Dutch East Indies Civil Aviation
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war civil airfield southeast of Pontianak
properties.notes: Served West Borneo civil/administrative flights alongside the nearby MLD seaplane base on the Kapuas River.
properties.title: Pontianak (Sungai Durian) Airfield

properties.name: Andir Airfield (Bandung)
properties.operator_1941: ML-KNIL (VLG-I HQ & Tech School) / KNILM main technical base
properties.runway_notes_1941: Major paved/grass military & civil aerodrome on Bandung plateau
properties.notes: Headquarters of ML-KNIL 1st Air Group (Martin 139 bombers), ML-KNIL Technical School, and KNILM's primary engineering base.
properties.title: Andir Airfield (Bandung)

properties.name: Kalidjati Airfield (Subang)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Oldest military airfield in Indonesia (built 1916); large grass/hard complex
properties.notes: Home to ML-KNIL Flight School and VkA-3, VkA-4, & VkA-5 reconnaissance squadrons; site of the Dutch surrender of Java in Mar 1942.
properties.title: Kalidjati Airfield (Subang)

properties.name: Tjililitan Airfield (Batavia)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Major military & civil airfield southeast of Batavia
properties.notes: Opened 1924; home to ML-KNIL 3rd Air Group (three squadrons of Martin 139 bombers) and original KNILM headquarters.
properties.title: Tjililitan Airfield (Batavia)

properties.name: Semplak Airfield (Buitenzorg)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Major fighter airbase northwest of Buitenzorg (Bogor)
properties.notes: Base of ML-KNIL 5th Air Group (Brewster 339D Buffalo fighters) defending West Java and Batavia.
properties.title: Semplak Airfield (Buitenzorg)

properties.name: Tjikembar Airfield (Sukabumi)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war West Java reconnaissance airfield
properties.notes: Base of ML-KNIL Verkenningsafdeling 1 (Curtiss-Wright CW-22 Falcon reconnaissance aircraft) on 30 Nov 1941.
properties.title: Tjikembar Airfield (Sukabumi)

properties.name: Tjisaoek (Cisauk) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Dispersal fighter/bomber grass strip west of Batavia
properties.notes: Pre-war ML-KNIL satellite and emergency dispersal airfield in West Java (Tangerang area).
properties.title: Tjisaoek (Cisauk) Airfield

properties.name: Tasikmalaya (Cibeureum) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war southeastern West Java military landing ground
properties.notes: ML-KNIL auxiliary airfield in Priangan highlands used for dispersal and training.
properties.modern_equivalent: Wiriadinata Air Force Base / Airport (TSY / WICM)
properties.title: Tasikmalaya (Cibeureum) Airfield

properties.name: Maguwo Airfield (Djokjakarta)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Opened 1940 as Central Java military airfield
properties.notes: Base of ML-KNIL Verkenningsafdeling 2 (CW-22 & Fokker C.X) on 30 Nov 1941.
properties.title: Maguwo Airfield (Djokjakarta)

properties.name: Maospati Airfield (Madiun)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Major East Java fighter airbase & aircraft depot (opened 1939)
properties.notes: Home to ML-KNIL 4th Air Group (Curtiss Hawk 75A-7 & CW-21B Interceptors) and ML-KNIL main aircraft depot.
properties.title: Maospati Airfield (Madiun)

properties.name: Singosari Airfield (Malang)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Major heavy bomber aerodrome near Malang (built 1937-40)
properties.notes: Base of ML-KNIL 2nd Air Group (Martin 139 bombers) and bomber flight school; later hosted USAAF B-17s in early 1942.
properties.title: Singosari Airfield (Malang)

properties.name: Ngoro (Blimbing) Secret Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Two 4,000-ft camouflaged sod runways with jungle dispersal taxiways
properties.notes: Pre-war ML-KNIL secret fighter airfield ~50 miles south of Surabaya; later hosted USAAF 17th Pursuit Squadron (Provisional) P-40s.
properties.title: Ngoro (Blimbing) Secret Airfield

properties.name: Perak Airfield (Surabaya)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Landplane aerodrome adjacent to Tandjong Perak port in Surabaya
properties.notes: Surabaya's primary military landplane field (distinct from the nearby Morokrembangan flying-boat base).
properties.title: Perak Airfield (Surabaya)

properties.name: Kemayoran Airport (Batavia)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Modern paved runways opened July 1940 as Batavia's flagship civil airport
properties.notes: Premier international civil airport of the Dutch East Indies (replaced Tjililitan for scheduled KLM/KNILM passenger traffic in 1940).
properties.title: Kemayoran Airport (Batavia)

properties.name: Darmo Airfield (Surabaya)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war civil grass/hard airport opened 1929
properties.notes: Surabaya's main pre-war KNILM commercial airport on the Batavia-Surabaya-Bali-Australia trunk route.
properties.title: Darmo Airfield (Surabaya)

properties.name: Semarang (Simongan / Kalibanteng) Airport
properties.runway_notes_1941: North-coast civil airport opened 1928 on KNILM Java trunk line
properties.notes: Regular daily KNILM commercial stop between Batavia, Bandung, and Surabaya.
properties.modern_equivalent: Jenderal Ahmad Yani International Airport (SRG / WAHS)
properties.title: Semarang (Simongan / Kalibanteng) Airport

properties.name: Tegal Airfield
properties.operator_1941: KNILM / Dutch East Indies Civil Aviation
properties.runway_notes_1941: Intermediate north-coast civil landing ground
properties.notes: Pre-war civil emergency and regional landing strip on the Batavia-Semarang air corridor.
properties.title: Tegal Airfield

properties.name: Cheribon (Penggung) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war civil landing field south of Cheribon (Cirebon)
properties.notes: Pre-war coastal civil airfield linking Batavia/Bandung with Central Java.
properties.title: Cheribon (Penggung) Airfield

properties.name: Tjilatjap (Cilacap) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war south-coast civil landing ground near Java's sole major Indian Ocean port
properties.notes: Pre-war civil strip near Tjilatjap harbor, later a crucial Allied evacuation port in Feb-Mar 1942.
properties.title: Tjilatjap (Cilacap) Airfield

properties.name: Palembang P1 (Talang Betutu) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Major civil & military airfield northwest of Palembang oil refineries
properties.notes: Opened 1920s as KNILM/KLM trunk stop and upgraded into primary Allied air defense base for Sumatra's oilfields; target of Japanese paratroop drop Feb 1942.
properties.modern_equivalent: Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin II International Airport (PLM / WIPP)
properties.title: Palembang P1 (Talang Betutu) Airfield

properties.name: Palembang P2 (Prabumulih / Karang Endah)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Camouflaged secret jungle airfield constructed in 1941 SW of Palembang
properties.notes: Built in 1941 as a secret heavy bomber base hidden in jungle near Karang Endah; entered operational ML-KNIL use in late Dec 1941.
properties.modern_equivalent: Defunct (Karang Endah, Muara Enim / Prabumulih, South Sumatra)
properties.title: Palembang P2 (Prabumulih / Karang Endah)

properties.name: Medan (Polonia) Airport
properties.runway_notes_1941: Opened 1928; major international civil airport for North Sumatra
properties.notes: Primary KLM Amsterdam-Batavia and KNILM Sumatra trunk airport serving the Deli plantation region.
properties.modern_equivalent: Soewondo Air Force Base / Former Polonia Airport (WIMK)
properties.title: Medan (Polonia) Airport

properties.name: Kutaraja (Blang Bintang) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Built 1936 near Koetaradja (Banda Aceh) at Sumatra's northern tip
properties.notes: Northernmost Dutch East Indies land airfield guarding the western approach to the Malacca Strait.
properties.modern_equivalent: Sultan Iskandar Muda International Airport (BTJ / WITT)
properties.title: Kutaraja (Blang Bintang) Airfield

properties.name: Sabang Airfield (Weh Island)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war island landing ground above Sabang coaling port
properties.notes: Guarded the strategic deepwater port of Sabang at the northern entrance to the Strait of Malacca.
properties.title: Sabang Airfield (Weh Island)

properties.name: Padang (Tabing) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Opened 1937 on West Sumatra coast north of Padang
properties.notes: Principal West Sumatra civil airport and Allied staging field along Sumatra's Indian Ocean flank.
properties.modern_equivalent: Sutan Sjahrir Air Force Base / Former Tabing Airport (WIMG)
properties.title: Padang (Tabing) Airfield

properties.name: Pekanbaru (Simpang Tiga) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Built 1930s in central Sumatra (Riau)
properties.notes: Pre-war central Sumatra civil and staging airfield connecting Medan, Palembang, and Singapore.
properties.modern_equivalent: Sultan Syarif Kasim II International Airport (PKU / WIBB)
properties.title: Pekanbaru (Simpang Tiga) Airfield

properties.name: Jambi (Paal Merah) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war civil & oil-district airfield southeast of Jambi
properties.notes: Served KNILM regional routes and Dutch oil exploration in central-southern Sumatra.
properties.title: Jambi (Paal Merah) Airfield

properties.name: Tanjung Karang (Branti) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war southern Sumatra airfield north of Teluk Betung
properties.notes: Strategic Sunda Strait airfield linking southern Sumatra and West Java.
properties.modern_equivalent: Radin Inten II International Airport (TKG / WILL)
properties.title: Tanjung Karang (Branti) Airfield

properties.name: Pangkal Pinang Airfield (Bangka)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war civil airport serving Bangka Island tin mines
properties.notes: Regular KNILM commercial destination between Batavia, Palembang, and Singapore.
properties.title: Pangkal Pinang Airfield (Bangka)

properties.name: Tanjung Pandan (Buluh Tumbang) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war civil & auxiliary airfield on Belitung (Billiton) Island
properties.notes: Served KNILM flights to Belitung tin mines and functioned as an Allied staging field across the Karimata Strait.
properties.title: Tanjung Pandan (Buluh Tumbang) Airfield

properties.name: Bengkulu (Padang Kemiling) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war southwestern Sumatra civil landing ground
properties.notes: Colonial civil landing strip on Sumatra's Indian Ocean coast serving Bencoolen (Bengkulu).
properties.title: Bengkulu (Padang Kemiling) Airfield

properties.name: Manado I (Mapanget) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war civil airfield northeast of Manado
properties.notes: Designated Manado I; pre-war northern Celebes civil airport defended by KNIL forces alongside Manado II (Langoan) in Jan 1942.
properties.title: Manado I (Mapanget) Airfield

properties.name: Manado II (Langoan / Kalawiran) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Inland Minahasa military airfield south of Lake Tondano (built late 1930s)
properties.notes: Designated Manado II; strategic northern Celebes military airfield and target of Japan's first-ever paratroop assault (1st Yokosuka SNLF) on 11 Jan 1942.
properties.title: Manado II (Langoan / Kalawiran) Airfield

properties.name: Kendari II Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Constructed 1937-1941; one of the finest all-weather military airbases in the NEI
properties.notes: Highly prized strategic bomber base commanding the Banda Sea and Java approaches; captured by Japan Jan 1942 and used to bomb Darwin and Surabaya.
properties.modern_equivalent: Haluoleo Airport / Air Force Base (KDI / WAWW)
properties.title: Kendari II Airfield

properties.name: Makassar (Mandai) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Opened 1937 north of Makassar (Maros)
properties.notes: Principal southern Celebes military and KNILM civil airfield commanding the southern Makassar Strait.
properties.title: Makassar (Mandai) Airfield

properties.name: Denpasar (Tuban) Airport
properties.runway_notes_1941: Opened 1937 on southern Bali isthmus
properties.notes: Key KNILM commercial stop on the Batavia-Surabaya-Kupang-Sydney air route; captured by Japan in Feb 1942.
properties.modern_equivalent: I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport (DPS / WADD)
properties.title: Denpasar (Tuban) Airport

properties.name: Rambang Airfield (Lombok)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war east-coast Lombok emergency/staging grass strip
properties.notes: Pre-war Dutch colonial staging and emergency landing ground along the Java-Timor-Australia air ferry route.
properties.title: Rambang Airfield (Lombok)

properties.name: Waingapu (Mau Hau) Airfield
properties.operator_1941: KNILM / Dutch East Indies Civil Aviation
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war Sumba civil/emergency landing strip
properties.notes: Intermediate staging strip between Bali/Lombok and Timor on the NEI-Australia air ferry route.
properties.title: Waingapu (Mau Hau) Airfield

properties.name: Kupang (Penfui) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Opened 1928; vital all-weather airfield on Dutch West Timor
properties.notes: Critical stepping-stone between Australia (Darwin) and Java for KNILM/Qantas civil airliners and Allied bombers; RAAF No. 2 Sqn Hudsons deployed Dec 1941.
properties.title: Kupang (Penfui) Airfield

properties.name: Dili Airfield
properties.operator_1941: Portuguese Colonial Administration / Qantas & Dai Nippon Airways (1941 survey)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Coastal grass/dirt civil landing strip west of Dili
properties.notes: Pre-war civil landing field in neutral Portuguese Timor used by Qantas Empire flights and pre-war Japanese survey flights from Palau.
properties.modern_equivalent: Presidente Nicolau Lobato International Airport (DIL / WPDL)
properties.title: Dili Airfield

properties.name: Laha Airfield (Ambon)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Built 1940-41 on north shore of Ambon Bay
properties.notes: Strategic eastern NEI landplane base (separate from Halong seaplane base); ML-KNIL Brewster fighters arrived 3 Dec 1941, joined by RAAF Hudsons.
properties.title: Laha Airfield (Ambon)

properties.name: Namlea Airfield (Buru)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war Dutch colonial auxiliary military landing strip on Buru Island
properties.notes: Emergency and forward staging land strip west of Ambon supporting Molucca Sea air patrols.
properties.title: Namlea Airfield (Buru)

properties.name: Babo Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Constructed 1936 by oil consortium; upgraded by ML-KNIL in 1941
properties.notes: Easternmost operational ML-KNIL land airfield in the Dutch East Indies (Bintuni Bay, Vogelkop); staged RAAF & Dutch patrols in late 1941.
properties.title: Babo Airfield

properties.name: Tan Son Nhut Airfield (Saigon)
properties.operator_1941: IJNAS 22nd Air Flotilla / Vichy Armee de l'Air / Air France
properties.runway_notes_1941: Major international paved/laterite airbase north of Saigon
properties.notes: Premier pre-war Air France & Armee de l'Air hub; occupied July 1941 by Japan and used by Genzan/Mihoro Kokutai G3M/G4M bombers to sink Force Z (10 Dec 1941).
properties.modern_equivalent: Tan Son Nhat International Airport (SGN / VVTS)
properties.title: Tan Son Nhut Airfield (Saigon)

properties.name: Bien Hoa Airfield
properties.operator_1941: Vichy Armee de l'Air / Imperial Japanese Army Air Service (IJAAS)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Major military airbase northeast of Saigon
properties.notes: Pre-war French Armee de l'Air base occupied by Japanese air units in July 1941 to support the Malaya campaign.
properties.title: Bien Hoa Airfield

properties.name: Thu Dau Mot Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Military bomber airfield north of Saigon (expanded late 1941)
properties.notes: Occupied by Japan July 1941; major launch base for IJNAS G4M1 'Betty' and G3M2 'Nell' bombers attacking Singapore and Force Z in Dec 1941.
properties.modern_equivalent: Defunct (Phu Loi / Thu Dau Mot, Binh Duong)
properties.title: Thu Dau Mot Airfield

properties.name: Soc Trang Airfield
properties.operator_1941: IJNAS / IJAAS (3rd Air Division) / Vichy France
properties.runway_notes_1941: Southern Mekong Delta military airbase
properties.notes: Occupied by Japan July 1941; critical forward base for IJNAS A6M Zeroes and bombers covering the 8 Dec 1941 Malaya invasion fleet.
properties.title: Soc Trang Airfield

properties.name: Phu Quoc (Duong Dong) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Forward island fighter staging strip in Gulf of Thailand
properties.notes: Prepared in late 1941 as the closest Indochinese fighter strip to Thailand and northern Malaya (launched Ki-27/Ki-43 escort sorties 8 Dec 1941).
properties.modern_equivalent: Defunct (Old Duong Dong Airport, Phu Quoc)
properties.title: Phu Quoc (Duong Dong) Airfield

properties.name: Tourane (Da Nang) Airfield
properties.operator_1941: Vichy Armee de l'Air / Imperial Japan / Air France
properties.runway_notes_1941: Major central Annam coastal airfield (built 1930s)
properties.notes: Key military and Air France relay base midway between Hanoi and Saigon; occupied by Japanese forces in July 1941.
properties.title: Tourane (Da Nang) Airfield

properties.name: Nha Trang Airfield
properties.operator_1941: Vichy Armee de l'Air / Imperial Japan
properties.runway_notes_1941: Coastal military & civil airfield in southern Annam
properties.notes: Occupied by Japan in July 1941 to provide air cover over Cam Ranh Bay invasion convoy staging area.
properties.title: Nha Trang Airfield

properties.name: Hanoi — Bach Mai Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Main French colonial military airbase in Hanoi (opened 1918)
properties.notes: Primary Armee de l'Air Tonkin airbase; used by Japanese air forces after the Sept 1940 Northern Indochina occupation.
properties.modern_equivalent: Defunct (Bach Mai / Truong Chinh area, Hanoi)
properties.title: Hanoi — Bach Mai Airfield

properties.name: Tong Airfield (Son Tay)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war French colonial military bomber/training airfield west of Hanoi
properties.notes: Major Armee de l'Air training and garrison airfield in the Red River Delta.
properties.title: Tong Airfield (Son Tay)

properties.name: Haiphong — Cat Bi Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Built 1930s serving Tonkin's principal seaport
properties.notes: Occupied by Japan in Sept 1940; key staging base for operations against southern China and northern Indochina.
properties.title: Haiphong — Cat Bi Airfield

properties.name: Phu Tho Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Red River valley military landing field NW of Hanoi
properties.notes: One of the specific Tonkin airfields ceded to Japanese air use under the September 1940 Nishihara-Decoux accord.
properties.title: Phu Tho Airfield

properties.name: Kompong Trach Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Forward southern Cambodia bomber/fighter base expanded late 1941
properties.notes: Major IJAAS 3rd Air Division launch airfield in Dec 1941 for strikes on northern Malaya airfields (Alor Star, Sungei Patani, Kota Bharu).
properties.title: Kompong Trach Airfield

properties.name: Kompong Chhnang Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Central Cambodia military airfield south of Tonle Sap
properties.notes: Pre-war French military airfield used in the 1940-41 Franco-Thai War and occupied by IJAAS in late 1941.
properties.title: Kompong Chhnang Airfield

properties.name: Siem Reap Airfield
properties.operator_1941: IJAAS (3rd Air Division) / Vichy France / Civil Angkor flights
properties.runway_notes_1941: Opened 1932 near Angkor; expanded for military use 1940-41
properties.notes: Active during Franco-Thai War (Jan 1941) and occupied by Japan July 1941 as a major IJAAS staging base for Thailand and Malaya.
properties.title: Siem Reap Airfield

properties.name: Battambang Airfield
properties.subregion: Cambodia (Phra Tabong, ceded to Thailand May 1941)
properties.territory_1941: Kingdom of Thailand (ceded from French Indochina May 1941)
properties.operator_1941: Royal Thai Air Force (formerly French Armee de l'Air)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war French colonial airfield in western Cambodia
properties.notes: Built by France in the 1930s; transferred to Thailand in May 1941 following the Franco-Thai War and used by IJAAS in Dec 1941.
properties.title: Battambang Airfield

properties.name: Hanoi — Gia Lam Airport
properties.control_dec_1941: Vichy France / Imperial Japan (shared from Sept 1940)
properties.operator_1941: Air France / Civil Aviation (IJAAS occupied Sept 1940)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Opened 1936 across the Red River as Hanoi's international civil airport
properties.notes: Terminus of Air France's Paris-Bangkok-Hanoi-Hong Kong commercial trunk route; occupied by Japanese troops on 26 Sept 1940.
properties.title: Hanoi — Gia Lam Airport

properties.name: Hue (Phu Bai) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Opened 1940 southeast of imperial capital Hue
properties.notes: Constructed by the French colonial administration in 1940 to serve the imperial court and administration in Hue.
properties.title: Hue (Phu Bai) Airfield

properties.name: Vinh Airfield
properties.operator_1941: French Colonial Civil Aviation / Air France
properties.runway_notes_1941: Built 1937 as coastal intermediate civil airfield
properties.notes: Served northern Annam on the Hanoi-Tourane-Saigon colonial air mail route.
properties.title: Vinh Airfield

properties.name: Phan Thiet Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war coastal civil landing ground in southern Annam
properties.notes: Intermediate coastal airfield between Saigon and Nha Trang; accessible to Japanese aircraft after July 1941.
properties.title: Phan Thiet Airfield

properties.name: Dalat (Cam Ly) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Highland civil airstrip serving the French hill station of Dalat
properties.notes: Pre-war colonial administrative and resort civil airfield in the Central Highlands.
properties.title: Dalat (Cam Ly) Airfield

properties.name: Phnom Penh (Pochentong) Airport
properties.operator_1941: Air France / Colonial Civil Aviation (IJAAS from July 1941)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Cambodia's primary pre-war civil airport west of Phnom Penh
properties.notes: Opened in the 1930s for civil mail/passenger service linking Saigon and Bangkok; occupied by Japanese forces in July 1941.
properties.title: Phnom Penh (Pochentong) Airport

properties.name: Vientiane (Wattay) Airfield
properties.operator_1941: Air France / French Colonial Civil Aviation
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war Mekong valley civil airport west of Vientiane
properties.notes: Principal civil airport of French Laos, served by Air France's Bangkok-Vientiane-Hanoi route.
properties.title: Vientiane (Wattay) Airfield

properties.name: Seno (Savannakhet) Airfield
properties.operator_1941: French Colonial Civil Aviation / Armee de l'Air transit
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war central Laos civil & colonial transit airfield
properties.notes: Key Mekong corridor landing ground in central Laos used for colonial mail and administrative flights.
properties.title: Seno (Savannakhet) Airfield

properties.name: Luang Prabang Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war northern Laos royal-capital landing strip
properties.notes: Colonial civil landing field linking the royal capital of Luang Prabang with Vientiane and Hanoi.
properties.title: Luang Prabang Airfield

properties.name: Pakse Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war southern Laos civil landing field on the Mekong
properties.notes: Served southern Laos colonial administration and airmail routes connecting to Saigon and Phnom Penh.
properties.title: Pakse Airfield

properties.name: Don Muang Airfield (Bangkok)
properties.operator_1941: Royal Thai Air Force HQ / Imperial Airways, KLM, Air France, Aerial Transport Co.
properties.runway_notes_1941: Opened 1914; major all-weather military & international civil airport north of Bangkok
properties.notes: HQ of the Royal Thai Air Force and Bangkok's international civil hub; Thai fighters engaged Japanese aircraft here on 8 Dec 1941 prior to the ceasefire.
properties.modern_equivalent: Don Mueang International Airport / RTAF Base (DMK / VTBD)
properties.title: Don Muang Airfield (Bangkok)

properties.name: Kok Kathiem Airfield (Lopburi)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Opened 1938 as major modern RTAF airbase
properties.notes: Major Royal Thai Air Force combat base in central Thailand; home to Wing 2 fighter and bomber squadrons.
properties.modern_equivalent: Khok Kathiam Air Force Base (KKM / VTBL)
properties.title: Kok Kathiem Airfield (Lopburi)

properties.name: Prachuap Khiri Khan (Ao Manao) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Coastal military airfield at Ao Manao Bay
properties.notes: Home to RTAF Wing 5; site of the fierce 8-9 Dec 1941 Battle of Prachuap Khiri Khan against Japanese landing troops.
properties.modern_equivalent: Prachuap Khiri Khan RTAF Base (Wing 5 / VTBP)
properties.title: Prachuap Khiri Khan (Ao Manao) Airfield

properties.name: Nakhon Ratchasima (Korat) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Major northeastern RTAF airbase on Khorat Plateau
properties.notes: Key RTAF base during the 1940-41 Franco-Thai War and hub of early Aerial Transport Co. mail routes.
properties.modern_equivalent: Korat Royal Thai Air Force Base (VTUN)
properties.title: Nakhon Ratchasima (Korat) Airfield

properties.name: Ubon Ratchathani Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Major eastern RTAF airbase facing French Laos & Cambodia
properties.notes: Primary RTAF forward bomber/fighter base during the 1940-41 Franco-Thai War; also served civil airmail flights.
properties.modern_equivalent: Ubon Ratchathani Airport / RTAF Wing 21 (UBP / VTUU)
properties.title: Ubon Ratchathani Airfield

properties.name: Udon Thani Airfield
properties.operator_1941: Royal Thai Air Force / Aerial Transport Co. of Thailand
properties.runway_notes_1941: Northeastern RTAF & civil airmail airfield near the Mekong
properties.notes: Active pre-war RTAF airfield and commercial stop on the Korat-Udon-Nakhon Phanom civil mail network.
properties.modern_equivalent: Udon Thani International Airport / RTAF Wing 23 (UTH / VTUD)
properties.title: Udon Thani Airfield

properties.name: Lampang Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Grass military landing ground (4,920 x 8,100 ft field, 2 hangars; US Survey 1941)
properties.notes: Classified as an RTAF military landing ground in the March 1941 US Survey; major base for RTAF Wing 80 and IJAAF 77th Sentai in late Dec 1941.
properties.title: Lampang Airfield

properties.name: Chanthaburi Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war southeastern Thai military airfield
properties.notes: Base of RTAF 22nd (Corsair) & 41st (Hawk III) Squadrons in 1941 prior to their northern redeployment in late Dec 1941.
properties.title: Chanthaburi Airfield

properties.name: Prachinburi Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war eastern frontier military landing ground
properties.notes: RTAF forward staging airfield east of Bangkok used during the 1940-41 Franco-Thai border conflict.
properties.title: Prachinburi Airfield

properties.name: Aranyaprathet (Wattana Nakhon) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Frontier military landing ground along Bangkok-Cambodia rail corridor
properties.notes: Key RTAF forward fighter strip during the 1940-41 Franco-Thai War.
properties.title: Aranyaprathet (Wattana Nakhon) Airfield

properties.name: Songkhla (Singora) Airfield
properties.operator_1941: Royal Thai Air Force / Civil (IJAAS from 8 Dec 1941)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Strategic coastal airfield on Gulf of Thailand just north of Malaya
properties.notes: Primary objective of Japan's 5th Division landing on 8 Dec 1941; immediately became IJAAS's main forward base attacking northern Malaya.
properties.title: Songkhla (Singora) Airfield

properties.name: Pattani (Bo Thong) Airfield
properties.operator_1941: Royal Thai Air Force / Civil (IJAAS from 8 Dec 1941)
properties.runway_notes_1941: Southern Thai landing ground near Pattani Bay
properties.notes: Seized during Japanese amphibious landing on 8 Dec 1941; operational Japanese fighter strip by 9 Dec 1941.
properties.title: Pattani (Bo Thong) Airfield

properties.name: Nakhon Si Thammarat (Cha Eian) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Southern Kra Isthmus military landing ground
properties.notes: Pre-war southern Thai airfield and site of one of the Japanese coastal landings on 8 Dec 1941.
properties.title: Nakhon Si Thammarat (Cha Eian) Airfield

properties.name: Tak (Rahaeng) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war western frontier landing ground near the Ping River
properties.notes: Used as forward staging field on the Burma approach; IJAAF 77th Sentai Ki-27 fighters deployed here in Dec 1941 before moving to Lampang.
properties.title: Tak (Rahaeng) Airfield

properties.name: Nakhon Sawan (Pak Nam Pho) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war central Chao Phraya valley airfield
properties.notes: Strategic central Thailand junction airfield linking Bangkok with northern airfields.
properties.title: Nakhon Sawan (Pak Nam Pho) Airfield

properties.name: Chiang Mai Airfield
properties.operator_1941: Aerial Transport Co. of Thailand / RTAF
properties.runway_notes_1941: Opened 1921 (Suthep); northern railhead civil airport
properties.notes: Principal northern Thai civil airport linking Chiang Mai with Bangkok, Mae Hong Son, and Chiang Rai; also used by RTAF & IJAAF from late Dec 1941.
properties.title: Chiang Mai Airfield

properties.name: Chiang Rai (Old) Airfield
properties.operator_1941: Aerial Transport Co. of Thailand / RTAF
properties.runway_notes_1941: Established 1924 south of Chiang Rai town
properties.notes: Pre-war far-northern Thai airmail and RTAF staging field near the Shan States (Burma) border.
properties.title: Chiang Rai (Old) Airfield

properties.name: Mae Hong Son Airstrip
properties.runway_notes_1941: Opened 1939 as remote mountain civil airmail strip
properties.notes: Built to provide commercial airmail and passenger access to Thailand's remote northwestern border valley; confirmed operational in 1940-41 US War Dept. surveys.
properties.title: Mae Hong Son Airstrip

properties.name: Phrae Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war northern civil airmail landing ground
properties.notes: Regular stop on the pre-war Bangkok-Phitsanulok-Phrae-Chiang Mai civil airmail route.
properties.title: Phrae Airfield

properties.name: Phitsanulok Airfield
properties.operator_1941: Aerial Transport Co. of Thailand / RTAF
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war commercial & airmail junction airfield
properties.notes: Important pre-war Aerial Transport Co. of Thailand hub connecting Bangkok with northern Thailand.
properties.title: Phitsanulok Airfield

properties.name: Khon Kaen Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war Isan civil airmail landing field
properties.notes: Regular stop on the Aerial Transport Co. of Thailand's northeastern commercial airmail network (opened 1931).
properties.title: Khon Kaen Airfield

properties.name: Roi Et Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war Isan civil airmail landing field
properties.notes: Early Aerial Transport Co. of Thailand airmail stop linking Korat with Nakhon Phanom and Ubon.
properties.title: Roi Et Airfield

properties.name: Surat Thani (Bandon) Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war Kra Isthmus civil landing ground near Bandon Bay
properties.notes: Pre-war southern civil landing strip on the peninsula corridor; near Japanese landing site on 8 Dec 1941.
properties.modern_equivalent: Surat Thani International Airport / RTAF Wing 7 (URT / VTSB)
properties.title: Surat Thani (Bandon) Airfield

properties.name: Phuket Airfield
properties.operator_1941: Aerial Transport Co. of Thailand / Civil Aviation
properties.runway_notes_1941: Opened 1933 on northwestern Phuket Island
properties.notes: Pre-war southern civil airport serving Phuket's tin-mining industry and Bangkok-Penang regional connections.
properties.title: Phuket Airfield

properties.name: Hua Hin Airfield
properties.runway_notes_1941: Pre-war coastal civil & royal-resort landing ground
properties.notes: Pre-war coastal civil strip along the upper Gulf of Thailand railway corridor.
properties.title: Hua Hin Airfield
